contract: Socket.IO outgoing stream_error: a transcode that fails emits {id: session id, error: non-empty text} once on every socket of the owning user and no other socket, removes the stream folder and emits no stream_open or stream_closed; a healthy stream, a repeated request after the failure and another user's sockets receive no stream_error.
exceptions: force is not applicable: stream errors are produced by the transcode process; there is no API that forces one.

The error text is asserted only as a non-empty string with exactly the id and error fields: upstream includes an internal input path in the message, the accepted Go difference uses fixed safe text, and no client parses the text (the web client reads an errorMessage field upstream never sends).
The accepted playback lifecycle packet supplies scoped evidence; its documented Go differences (fixed safe text, immediate reaping of the exited process) are deliberately not asserted here.

invariants.contract: A transcode that fails on its input emits stream_error exactly once on both sockets of the owner with exactly the fields id (the session id) and error (a non-empty string), emits no stream_open and no stream_closed, removes the metadata/streams/<id> folder and leaves the HLS route at 404.

A successful transcode that completes and serves segments emits no stream_error; repeating the HLS requests of a failed stream answers 404 with no second stream_error; a failed stream of one user reaches none of another user's sockets while that user's stream keeps serving segments.
